Focus on Productivity & Employment Growth,

Each of Which Accounts for ~50% of Long-Term Real GDP Growth

e Investments in Technology / Infrastructure / Education Boost Productivity.
— Newer technology improves efficiency of communication and lowers costs of providing goods and services.
— Better infrastructure reduces transportation costs for input and output materials — Better education improves general labor quality and enables specialization for more efficiency.

e Removing Restrictions / Uncertainties in Various Regulations Can Stimulate Private Employment.

— Immigration does not reduce employment opportunities for US-born workers, per Federal Reserve study in 8/10.

— Removing tax / regulatory uncertainty could help create hiring incentives for private industries.

e Hours Worked per Worker Have Remained Steady at ~39-40 Hours per Week From 1970 to 2009 and Will Likely Remain Steady.

Source: OECD, Dale W. Jorgenson, Mun S. Ho, Kevin J. Stiroh, "Growth of U.S. industries and Investments in Information Technology and Higher Education" http:/Avwww.nber.org/chapters/c1 0627, Federal Reserve.
